summary: Iteration 4 (frontend only): retested the fix for address suggestions being cut off on mobile. At 390x844, the dropdowns for input-waypoint-0 ('via rizzoli bologna'), input-origin ('via del corso roma') and input-destination ('piazza san marco venezia') are positioned against the StopRow root. They run from the marker column to the card's right edge (left=33, right=357, width=324px), while the inputs are only 120-190px wide. Measured spans: scrollWidth<=clientWidth for all of them, so no text is cut off and there is no ellipsis. Long labels wrap onto 2 lines. No horizontal page overflow. elementFromPoint confirms the dropdown sits above the next row. Clicking suggestion-0 fills the input with the exact label and closes the dropdown. With the destination dropdown open, all 4 items stay above the fixed ActionBar (last item bottom 703 < bar top 720) and can still be clicked after scrolling. Desktop 1920: same behaviour, dropdown width 580px (full row), single-line labels, pick and close work. All features pass.

issues: The waypoint input is only ~120px wide (GPS + up/down/remove buttons take the rest), so a selected address shows as 'Via Francesc...' inside the input. This is acceptable, but a 2-line layout for the control buttons on mobile would make the chosen value easier to read (optional).

critical_code_review_comments: AddressInput's <ul absolute> now depends on the nearest positioned ancestor being StopRow's 'relative' root. This is an implicit coupling: if AddressInput is reused somewhere else without a relative parent, the dropdown will be positioned against an unexpected ancestor. Consider documenting it or passing in a container ref.
There is still no keyboard navigation (arrow keys/Enter) and no loading indicator for suggestions.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suggestions come from Photon via /api/route/suggest (debounce 350ms). At 390px, check the dropdown width against the closest('.relative') StopRow root rect, and check truncation via span.scrollWidth > clientWidth. The ActionBar overlay from iteration 3 now looks fixed: the bar is on top and the dropdown items are not covered.
